zh.title: 波音737 MAX、787與777X翼尖設計大不同：同一減阻目標的三種工程取捨
zh.summary: 波音最新三款民航機都想降低誘導阻力、節省燃油，卻採用截然不同的翼尖設計：737 MAX用分叉式翼梢小翼，787用後掠式翼尖，777X則用可折疊翼尖，差異來自機場尺寸限制與各自的設計條件。
body: 波音最新三款民航機波音737 MAX、787夢幻客機與777X的共同目標，都是降低空氣阻力、提升燃油效率，但三者的翼尖設計卻截然不同。機翼上下方的氣壓差會在翼尖形成渦流，產生誘導阻力，拉長翼展是最直接的解法，但國際民航組織依翼展劃分機場使用類別，機翼過長會限制飛機可用的登機門與滑行道，製造商必須在氣動效率與機場相容性之間取捨。

波音737 MAX採用分叉式先進技術翼梢小翼，一片向上、一片向下，在不大幅增加翼展的情況下降低誘導阻力，關鍵在於維持與737次世代機隊的共通性，將翼展控制在國際民航組織C類上限118英尺、約36米以內。波音787則是全新設計的廣體機，擁有較大的設計自由度，採用細長後掠式翼尖直接延伸翼展，波音與美國國家航空暨太空總署的研究顯示，後掠式翼尖可降低阻力約5.5%，優於傳統翼梢小翼約3.5%至4.5%的效果；787機翼以碳纖維複合材料打造，輕量且具彈性。波音777X的翼展全展達235英尺、約72米，是現役設計中最大的民航機翼展，透過可折疊翼尖在地面將翼展縮至略低於213英尺、約65米，符合E類機場尺寸要求，起飛前再展開恢復完整氣動構型。777X原訂2020年投入服務，因認證挑戰與GE9X發動機問題多次延誤，波音目前目標2027年交付首架777-9，777-8F約兩年後交付，777-8客機則不早於2030年；阿聯酋航空以270架訂單居首，卡達航空124架、韓航40架、國泰35架、新航31架。

en.title: Why Boeing's 737 MAX, 787 and 777X have such different wingtip designs
en.summary: Boeing's three most modern airliners share one goal, reducing drag and improving fuel efficiency, but use strikingly different wingtips: split-tip winglets on the 737 MAX, swept-back raked wingtips on the 787, and folding wingtips on the 777X. The differences come from airport size limits and each aircraft's design constraints.
body: Boeing's three most modern commercial aircraft, the 737 MAX, the 787 Dreamliner and the 777X, share a common objective: reducing aerodynamic drag and improving fuel efficiency. Yet their wingtip designs are noticeably different. As air moves around a wing, higher-pressure air beneath it moves toward the lower-pressure region above, creating swirling vortices at the wingtips that cause induced drag. Increasing wingspan is the most straightforward way to reduce it, but the International Civil Aviation Organization sets aircraft size categories largely by wingspan, so an aircraft that exceeds the relevant dimensions may need different airport facilities. Each design is therefore a compromise between aerodynamic efficiency and airport compatibility.

The Boeing 737 MAX uses Advanced Technology winglets with a split-tip configuration, one extension pointing upward and another extending downward, reducing induced drag without a substantial increase in wingspan. Keeping its wingspan within the ICAO Code C limit of 118 feet (36 meters) mattered because the MAX was developed to retain considerable operational commonality with the 737 Next Generation family. The Boeing 787, developed as an entirely new aircraft family, uses long, swept-back raked wingtips that extend the wing horizontally; research from Boeing and NASA indicates raked wingtips can reduce drag by approximately 5.5%, compared with around 3.5% to 4.5% for conventional winglets, and its composite wings are long, thin and flexible. The Boeing 777X goes further, with a wingspan of 235 feet (72 meters) when fully deployed, the largest of any commercial airliner currently designed for airline service, and folding wingtips that reduce the span to just under 213 feet (65 meters) on the ground, within Code E airport requirements, before extending again for take-off. The program has faced considerable delays: originally expected to enter service in 2020, it has dealt with certification challenges, flight-testing setbacks and issues with its GE9X engines, and Boeing is targeting the first 777-9 delivery in 2027, the 777-8F around two years later, and the passenger 777-8 not before 2030. Emirates is the largest 777X customer with 270 on order, followed by Qatar Airways with 124, Korean Air with 40, Cathay Pacific with 35 and Singapore Airlines with 31.

facts.claim: The Boeing 737 MAX, Boeing 787 Dreamliner and Boeing 777X share the objective of reducing aerodynamic drag and improving fuel efficiency, but feature noticeably different wingtip designs.
Wingtip vortices contribute to induced drag, and the International Civil Aviation Organization establishes aircraft size categories largely determined by wingspan, limiting how long wings can be.

The Boeing 737 MAX uses Advanced Technology winglets with a split-tip configuration, one extension pointing upward and another extending downward, keeping its wingspan within the ICAO Code C limit of 118 feet (36 meters).

The Boeing 787 uses long, swept-back raked wingtips, and research from Boeing and NASA indicates raked wingtips can reduce drag by approximately 5.5%, compared with around 3.5% to 4.5% for conventional winglets.
The Boeing 777X's wings extend 235 feet (72 meters) when fully deployed, and folding wingtips reduce the span to just under 213 feet (65 meters) on the ground, within Code E airport requirements.
The 777X was originally expected to enter service in 2020, and Boeing is targeting the first 777-9 delivery in 2027, the 777-8F around two years later, and the passenger 777-8 not before 2030.
Emirates has 270 777X aircraft on order, followed by Qatar Airways with 124, Korean Air with 40, Cathay Pacific with 35 and Singapore Airlines with 31.
